Understanding Metal Shingle Installation & Replacement

When planning a steep-slope residential roofing project, metal shingle installation encompasses both new construction installation and the complete tear-off and replacement of aging, weathered shingles down to the structural roof decking.

Our nationwide contractor referral network connects property owners with independent, verified roofing professionals who specialize in metal systems. From architectural layout and proper ventilation integration to code-compliant fastening patterns, every project is executed to deliver optimal weatherproofing and aesthetic curb appeal.

The 5-Step Professional Installation Process

A certified residential installation follows a rigorous engineering sequence to protect your home's building envelope:

  1. Complete Tear-Off & Deck Inspection: Removal of all existing roofing layers down to bare plywood or OSB sheathing. Damaged, delaminated, or rotted decking boards are replaced with new APA-rated sheathing.
  2. Eaves & Valley Water Barrier Installation: Application of self-adhering ice-and-water membranes along critical leak zones, including eaves, valleys, rakes, and chimney saddles.
  3. Synthetic Underlayment & Metal Drip Edge: High-tear-strength synthetic underlayment is rolled horizontally across the entire deck, complemented by corrosion-resistant metal drip edge installed along all perimeter roof edges.
  4. Precision Shingle Application: Shingles are installed using manufacturer-specified nail schedules (typically 4 to 6 fasteners per shingle) to ensure wind resistance compliance up to Up to 140–160 MPH.
  5. Ridge Ventilation & Magnetic Cleanup: Continuous ridge exhaust vents and matching hip/ridge cap shingles are secured, followed by multiple rolling magnetic sweeps across lawns, driveways, and landscaping to collect all loose nails.

Building Code & Fire Safety Compliance

Metal Shingle Installation must meet strict building standards under the International Residential Code (IRC Chapter 9). With a certified fire rating of Class A (Non-combustible) and an impact rating of Class 4 (Highest UL 2218 rating), this system provides dependable defense against windborne embers, hail strikes, and severe weather events.

Independent contractors in our network pull required municipal building permits, coordinate mid-deck or final building inspections, and ensure all installations adhere to local climate amendments.

Pros and Cons of Metal Shingles

Advantages

  • Exceptional 50 to 70-year service life outlasts standard asphalt by 2 to 3 times
  • Interlocking shingle profiles resist 140+ mph hurricane-force wind uplift
  • Class 4 impact rating resists severe golf-ball and tennis-ball sized hailstones
  • Extremely lightweight (under 170 lbs/square), minimizing structural roof load
  • Qualifies for maximum homeowner insurance policy discounts in storm states

Considerations & Drawbacks

  • Higher initial material and skilled installation investment than asphalt
  • Requires factory-matched trim and specialized bending tools at hips and valleys
  • Uncoated bare aluminum requires anti-corrosion considerations near saltwater surf

Comparing Metal to Alternative Shingle Materials

Before committing to an installation, explore how Metal compares to popular alternative roofing choices:

Asphalt Shingles

Metal shingles cost 2 to 3x more upfront than asphalt, but eliminate re-roofing cycles for over half a century.

Slate Shingles

Metal shingles emulate natural slate texture at one-seventh the structural weight, requiring zero framing reinforcement.

Planning Your Metal Roofing Budget?

Installed investment for metal shingles ranges from $850 – $1,400 per square. Pricing factors include roof square footage, slope pitch complexity, tear-off layer disposal, and plywood deck repairs.

Frequently Asked Questions About Metal Shingle Installation

Are metal shingle roofs noisy when it rains?

No. Because metal shingles are installed over solid wood roof decking and modern synthetic underlayment, attic insulation and drywall absorb acoustic vibrations. Sound levels inside the living space are indistinguishable from asphalt shingle roofs.

Can metal shingles withstand large hail without denting?

Stone-coated steel shingles carry a UL 2218 Class 4 impact rating, the highest possible benchmark. The textured stone granule coating conceals minor surface stresses while the resilient steel substrate resists puncture from 2-inch hailstones.

Will a metal shingle roof attract lightning strikes?

No. Metal does not attract lightning; lightning seeks the tallest grounded path to earth regardless of roof material. If struck, non-combustible metal shingles disperse electrical energy safely without catching fire.
